expectations.text: Classifies the CV screening/ranking tool as HIGH-RISK under Annex III point 4(a) (employment: recruitment or selection, incl. placing targeted job ads, analysing and filtering applications, evaluating candidates)
expectations.evidence: Response states 'Yes, this is high-risk... Annex III area: Area 4 — Employment, Workers Management, and Self-Employment, point (a) — Recruitment and selection... specifically "filtering or screening job applications" and "evaluat[ing] candidates."'

expectations.text: States the compliance deadline for Annex III standalone high-risk systems as 2 December 2027 (as amended by the Digital Omnibus, adopted June 2026; originally 2 August 2026). Any deadline stated must be 2 Dec 2027, not Aug 2026.
expectations.evidence: 'Annex III standalone high-risk systems must comply by 2 December 2027 (per the Digital Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force since 27 July 2026, which deferred the original 2 August 2026 date).'

expectations.text: Walks through core provider obligations citing Arts. 9-17 (risk management, data governance, technical documentation, logging, transparency to deployers, human oversight, accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity, QMS)
expectations.evidence: Table explicitly cites Art. 9 (risk management), Art. 10 (data governance), Art. 11 (technical documentation), Art. 12 (logging), Art. 13 (transparency to deployers), Art. 14 (human oversight), Art. 15 (accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity), Art. 16 (provider checklist), Art. 17 (QMS).

expectations.text: Mentions conformity assessment and registration: self-assessment per Annex VI for Annex III point 4 systems, EU declaration of conformity (Art. 47), CE marking (Art. 48), EU database registration (Art. 49)
expectations.evidence: Table: 'Conformity assessment | Art. 43 | Annex III Area 4 is a Points 2–8 area → self-assessment only (Annex VI-style internal control)...'; 'EU Declaration of Conformity | Art. 47...'; 'CE marking | Art. 48...'; 'EU AI database registration | Art. 49 | Register before placing the system on the market.'

expectations.text: Notes the Art. 6(3) derogation exists but explains it is narrow and does not apply where the system profiles natural persons / materially influences hiring decisions (profiling is always high-risk)
expectations.evidence: 'Art. 6(3) exceptions test: None of the narrow exceptions... plausibly apply — ranking applicants is the substantive evaluation, not a preparatory or narrow procedural step. Profiling override (Art. 6(3), final subparagraph): Even if an exception were argued, a CV-ranking tool profiles natural persons... which makes it high-risk regardless.'
